reasons.plausibility: The Hall-Petch mechanism is generally not effective at such high homologous temperatures (1273 K) because grain boundaries become sources/sinks for vacancies and sites for diffusional creep, making the predicted 40-60% strength improvement physically unsound.
reasons.testability: The proposed falsification test is clear, directly compares the new process to the baseline, and specifies a quantitative criterion (40% increase) with microstructural checks, though it omits a crucial grain size stability check during the high-temperature test itself.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it relies on a strengthening mechanism known to be ineffective at the target temperature, and the proposed test would likely fail, wasting resources without advancing the understanding of high-temperature strength in this alloy.
